draft.title: Health behaviours and risk factors
card: an action a person takes that affects their health, such as being active, eating well, sleeping enough, smoking or drinking alcohol.
anything that raises the chance of illness or injury. Smoking and a long-term lack of physical activity are examples.
Some behaviours lower the risk of illness. Regular physical activity, a varied diet and enough sleep are examples.
A risk factor raises the chance of illness but does not make it certain. Many risk factors together, over a long time, can add up.
draft.remember: Behaviours can raise or lower the chance of illness, but they do not decide it.

a.q: Which of these is a health behaviour that lowers the risk of illness?
opts: Walking to school most days of the week
Sleeping only four hours on school nights
Smoking one cigarette a day
Skipping meals to stay awake at night
a.why: Regular physical activity is a behaviour that lowers the risk of illness. The other three are behaviours that raise the risk, so they are risk factors, not protection.
a.clue: Which action makes illness less likely?

b.q: Dan, 17, sleeps five hours a night and drinks alcohol most weekends. His friend says he will definitely get sick. What is the best response?
opts: These behaviours raise his risk, but illness is not certain
These behaviours have no effect until he is an adult
Only smoking counts as a risk factor, so he is safe
Illness is certain because he has two risk factors
b.why: Poor sleep and alcohol use are risk factors, so they raise the chance of illness. A risk factor makes illness more likely but does not guarantee it, so saying it is certain is wrong.
b.clue: Does a risk factor make illness more likely or certain?

a.best: Walking to school most days of the week

b.best: These behaviours raise his risk, but illness is not certain

problems.detail: The clue 'Does a risk factor make illness more likely or certain?' narrows the choice to 'more likely' versus 'certain'. Only one option says 'raise his risk', so the clue almost hands students the answer.

check.summary: The content is accurate and both questions have one clear right answer. The clue for question b nearly gives the answer away and could be made less leading.

proposal.title: Health behaviours and risk factors
card: an action a person takes that affects their health, such as being active, eating well, sleeping enough, smoking or drinking alcohol.
anything that raises the chance of illness or injury. Smoking, drinking alcohol, too little sleep and a long-term lack of physical activity are examples.
Some behaviours lower the risk of illness. Regular physical activity, a varied diet and enough sleep are examples.
A risk factor raises the chance of illness but does not make it certain. Many risk factors together, over a long time, can add up.
proposal.remember: Behaviours can raise or lower the chance of illness, but they do not decide it.

a.q: Which of these is a health behaviour that lowers the risk of illness?
opts: Walking to school most days of the week
Sleeping only four hours on school nights
Smoking one cigarette every day
Skipping breakfast on most school days
a.why: Regular physical activity is a behaviour that lowers the risk of illness. Too little sleep and smoking are risk factors, and skipping meals is not a varied diet, so none of the others lowers the risk.
a.clue: Which action makes illness less likely?

b.q: Dan, 17, sleeps five hours a night and drinks alcohol most weekends. His friend says he will definitely get sick. What is the best response?
opts: These behaviours raise his risk, but illness is not certain
Sleep and alcohol affect his mood, not his chance of illness
Only smoking is a risk factor, so his health is not at risk
Illness is certain because he has two risk factors at once
b.why: Too little sleep and alcohol use are risk factors, so they raise the chance of illness. A risk factor makes illness more likely but does not guarantee it, so saying illness is certain goes too far.
b.clue: Think about what a risk factor actually changes.
